title: Estimating firm digitalization: A method for disaggregating sector-level digital intensity to firm-level
author: Mucha, Seppälä
materials: The final step is classification of firm-level revenue-weighted digital intensity scores into low, medium, and high digital intensity groups. This step is important because of two reasons. First, since the proposed method disaggregates sector level generalizations to firm level, it is an imperative to recognize that the assigned firm-level digital intensity scores cannot be considered as precise figures. Calvino and colleagues [6] report high level of within-sector heterogeneity for many of the digital intensity indicators they consider. Furthermore, they highlight that there can be many alternative ways to aggregate digital intensity indicators into a “global” indicator. This methodological ambiguity reflects the complexity of the underlying phenomenon. Given that digitalization itself is multifaceted, complex, and evolving we do not expect that a single method can fully capture that phenomenon. Second, the proposed method is intended for use with both ordinal and ratio sector-level digital intensity score scales. The lower information content in ordinal scales creates the requirement for simplification of the final method outputs. Overall, given the two reasons discussed above, we consider that the proposed method strikes the right balance between providing useful granularity and acceptable risk of misclassifying companies.(2)g(DIm)={Low,ifDIm≤Q13Mid,ifDIm>Q13∧DIm≤Q23High,otherwise

steps.title: Obtain revenue by industry code
steps.instruction: For each company collect revenue figures for each industry code. If revenue is reported by business segment, split each segment's revenue evenly across all industry codes assigned to that segment. Discard any records with negative revenue (e.g., inter‑segment eliminations). When a company does not provide segment‑level breakdown, use the total company revenue and assign it to the primary (or secondary) industry code(s) available for that firm.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve revenue data per business segment or per company.
If a segment maps to multiple industry codes, divide the segment revenue equally among those codes.
Remove records where the revenue amount is negative.
If no segment breakdown exists, allocate the total company revenue to the primary (or secondary) industry code(s).

steps.title: Convert industry codes via concordance
steps.instruction: Harmonize firm‑level industry codes with the sector‑level classification used for digital intensity scores. If the classifications differ, download an appropriate concordance (or correspondence) table (e.g., from the U.S. Census Bureau or Eurostat) and map firm codes to sector codes. When a source code maps to several target codes, split the firm’s revenue for that code evenly among the target codes. If some source codes have no match, either (1) apply an alternative concordance table or (2) generalize both source and target codes by dropping the last digit, merge duplicate records by summing their revenues, and re‑apply the generalized concordance. Repeat iteratively until all firm codes are matched.

substeps.instruction: Check whether firm‑ and sector‑level codes are already in the same system and revision; skip this step if they are.
Map each firm‑level code to the sector‑level code(s).
If a single firm code maps to multiple sector codes, divide the firm’s revenue for that code equally among the sector codes.

For unmapped firm codes, first try another concordance table; if still unmapped, drop the last digit of both source and target codes, aggregate duplicate firm records by summing revenues, and re‑apply the concordance.
Iterate the above until every firm code has a sector‑level counterpart.

steps.title: Map digital intensity scores
steps.instruction: Using the matched sector‑level industry codes, look up the corresponding sector digital intensity score (SDIi) for each firm‑level code from the reference dataset. Verify that no industry code lacks a digital intensity value; if any are missing, resolve the issue before proceeding.

steps.title: Calculate revenue‑weighted intensity
steps.instruction: For each company compute the revenue‑weighted digital intensity score (DIX) as the weighted average of sector scores: DIX = Σ_i (SDIi × R_i,X), where R_i,X is the share of the company’s total revenue that comes from industry i (expressed in the same classification system as SDIi).

steps.title: Classify firms into intensity groups
steps.instruction: Determine the 33rd (Q1) and 66th (Q2) percentiles of the reference sector‑level digital intensity scores. Classify each firm’s DIX as Low if DIX ≤ Q1, Mid if Q1 < DIX ≤ Q2, and High otherwise. Use the reference‑derived quantiles rather than the sample’s own distribution.

substeps.instruction: Calculate Q1 and Q2 from the sector‑level reference data.
Assign firms to Low, Mid, or High groups based on the DIX thresholds.
